criteria.criterion: The create-path mapper `_map_local_to_dc_fields` is pinned by VALUE for every key it emits — summary, description, issuetype, priority, status, assignee — including each lookup's DEFAULT-fallback branch and empty-string fallbacks. It emits NO project key.
Both DC sanitizer boundaries are pinned at-limit AND one-over, including the truncation suffix marker, for summary, description and comment.

The shared `OutboundFieldMapper.map_fields_to_remote` is exercised through `WikiTextCodec`, pinning description over WIKI_DESCRIPTION_LIMIT, non-str passthrough, title->summary, status and priority DC values. Not an ordering assertion.
DC's identity label form is pinned by value.

DC's probe branches are pinned by value through a seam that reaches the REAL classifier. FakeTransport must NOT be used. All four branches must be reached — PRESENT_RESOLVED, PRESENT_FILTERED, ARCHIVED_OR_MOVED, UNREACHABLE.

The probe pin also proves DC binds ITS OWN configured resolved_statuses rather than Cloud's hardcoded set — with a NON-DEFAULT set (e.g. frozenset({'Custom Resolved'})) asserting the cross-set discriminator.
Where Cloud and DC legitimately differ, the parametrization carries a DIFFERENT expected value per vendor — no assertion claims parity where the adapters correctly diverge.

[operator-attested] Every new pin is mutation-checked, with the mutation and resulting verdict recorded BOTH as a comment on this ticket in the format `MUTATED: <symbol> <old_value> -> <wrong_value>; FAILED: <test_id>`, AND as a module-level comment block in the test file.
`test_backend_characterization.py`'s existing Cloud assertions still pass UNEDITED (a parametrization that changes Cloud's expectations has broken its safety net).
